title: Implement a Resource Anomaly Detection Agent in CampusGuard EDU Monitor
description: CampusGuard EDU Monitor is a system monitoring tool for university IT infrastructure, written in C. It currently has agents for metrics, security, and backups. A recent series of outages caused by runaway processes has highlighted the need for proactive resource monitoring. This task involves developing a new agent, the 'Resource Anomaly Agent', which will detect sustained high CPU or memory usage and trigger an alert. The development will be split across three sessions to simulate a realistic, iterative workflow.

project_spec.name: CampusGuard EDU Monitor
project_spec.description:
CampusGuard EDU Monitor is a medium-scale, C-based system monitoring suite designed specifically for university computer-science programs.  The application does more than keep servers healthy; it teaches students how professional monitoring, log aggregation, security scanning, backup/recovery, and automated deployments are built using the Model-View-Controller (MVC) paradigm.

In practice, students interact with the "View" through a lightweight GTK or ncurses dashboard that visualizes real-time metrics and security alerts emitted by the Observer pattern.  Controllers route user requests—such as opening historical logs, starting a scan, or initiating a disaster-recovery drill—through a Chain-of-Responsibility that validates permissions, queues jobs on an Event-Driven message bus, and dispatches them across a simulated Service Mesh of micro-agents running on lab VMs.  The Models encapsulate log archives, scan results, backup snapshots, deployment manifests, and alert rules, stored in SQLite and exposed over an internal REST layer so that students can experiment with data-science tooling.  By packaging professional monitoring concepts into an educative sandbox, CampusGuard helps learners explore DevSecOps practices while studying clean MVC separation and advanced design patterns.
dependencies: glib (core utilities, event loop, GObject Observer implementation)
libcurl (HTTP interactions with external update feeds)
GTK 3 or ncurses (alternative graphical / terminal Views)
systemd-unit templates or Ansible playbooks (deployment_automation examples)
